bullets.title: FOMC Decision Today: ~25-35% Hike Odds Create Largest Meeting Surprise Since 1997
bullets.body: Prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket) and fed futures are pricing 23-35% probability of a 25bp hike at today's 2pm ET FOMC meeting — the highest uncertainty at a non-cut meeting since 1997 per Goldman Sachs. JPMorgan's base case (50% probability) is a hawkish hold with S&P 500 flat to -0.5%; dovish hold (28%) could lift +1%. Fed has abandoned forward guidance under Warsh in favor of data-dependence. Former Fed adviser Faust expects no hike; White House's Hassett says 'Warsh will do the right thing.'

bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 Enters Technical Correction; July Shaping Up as Worst Month Since Sept 2022
bullets.body: QQQ has dropped 10%+ from June all-time highs, entering a technical correction. At -9.5% MTD, July is on pace to be the Nasdaq 100's worst month since September 2022 (-10.6%), which marked the low of the 2022 bear market. The S&P 500 Equal Weight ($RSP) is breaking out to new all-time highs simultaneously, signaling a sharp rotation away from tech/growth toward broader market.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Sector Bloodbath: SOX -28-29% Since June 22 Peak; Record Selling Per Goldman
bullets.body: The SOX index is down 28-29% in 26 trading days since its June 22 peak, approaching the 32% decline seen in the first 24 days after the Dot Com peak in March 2000. Goldman traders report 'record selling' and 'violent derisking' in semis. Long semis was BofA's most crowded trade in its July fund manager survey — that unwind is now underway. SOXL (3x leveraged) is down 69% since June 22. Semiconductors and tech down ~28% in July vs. Chinese ETFs MCHI +7%, FXI +14%.

bullets.title: AI/Momentum Unwind Deepens: GS High-Beta Momentum Basket Down 37% on Month, Day 3 of De-Gross
bullets.body: Goldman's GSPRHIMO (high beta momentum pair) is down 5.7% today and 37% on the month, marking the largest 3-day de-gross on GS Prime records since November 2022. Market breadth has flipped negative with 357 S&P 500 names previously green now red. JPMorgan warns the next round of selling will spread beyond single stocks to broader indexes, citing AI/MOMO unwind and Chinese open-source/DUV competitive threats.

bullets.title: Goldman Warns: Buy Protection; Correlation-1 Macro Event Risk 'Creeping Higher'
bullets.body: Goldman's Flows team warns risks of a correlation-1 macro event are rising and recommends buying market protection. NVDA CDS hit an all-time peak, signaling elevated credit risk despite stock resilience. Investment-grade bond yields are near 22-year highs relative to S&P 500 earnings yields, with bond vigilantes reasserting market discipline.

bullets.title: Iran-US Escalation Spikes Oil 8%+ to $86; Crude Draw 7.2M Barrels vs +256K Expected
bullets.body: Trump vowed to hit Iran 'hard' after Iranian forces struck US targets in Jordan, driving crude oil up 8% above $86/barrel and European gas up 5.1%. EIA reported a 7.167M barrel crude drawdown (vs. +256K consensus) for the week ending July 24, with Cushing at its lowest since 2014 and the SPR declining 5.1M barrels to 307.6M. Brent touched $92. CENTCOM confirms Strait of Hormuz remains open with ~1,000 ships and 500M barrels transited since May.

bullets.title: Korean Market Crisis: $25B Retail Losses, Leveraged ETF Liquidation ~90% Complete Per JPM
bullets.body: South Korean retail investors lost up to $25B in the past month, with individuals aged 20-30 comprising ~62% of liquidated accounts. KOSPI realized volatility is at levels seen only during major historical crashes. JPMorgan says most leveraged ETFs have been liquidated and hedge fund deleveraging is ~90% complete; South Korea is capping single-stock leveraged ETF exposure for retail investors. The XIV structural analogy has been drawn widely.

bullets.title: BofA Clients Buying the Dip for Fourth Straight Week; Institutional Investors Leading
bullets.body: Despite the S&P 500 slipping 0.6% last week, BofA clients extended a four-consecutive-week equity buying streak with institutional investors posting their largest weekly net purchases. SPY also saw ~$1M OTM put sales and a $1.5B put wall at SPY 735, though gamma distribution is increasingly negative.

bullets.title: Fed Under Warsh Has Ended Forward Guidance; Now Fully Data-Dependent
bullets.body: Under Warsh, the Fed ended its forward guidance framework starting with the June meeting, reverting to pure data-dependence. 30-year yields have risen since the September 2024 50bp cut and hit a 19-year high of 5.18% in May 2026, contradicting conventional wisdom on rate cuts easing financial conditions. Today's decision will be the largest surprise at a non-rate-cut meeting since 1997 regardless of outcome.

bullets.title: White House: Downward Price Pressure Coming; No Justification for US Debt Downgrade
bullets.body: White House Senior Adviser Hassett stated the administration expects downward pressure on prices and sees no justification for a US debt downgrade, claiming the long-run budget trajectory is improving. The remarks came on CNBC ahead of the FOMC meeting.

bullets.title: Semis Equipment Cycle Structural Bull Case: WFE Could Hit $230B+ by 2028 vs $190-200B Consensus
bullets.body: A detailed analysis argues 2028 wafer fab equipment spending could exceed $230B if Top-5 equipment makers sell their planned capacity, vs. street consensus of $190-200B. AMAT can double output with floor space ready, Lam has nearly doubled capacity in four years, TEL targets 1.8x by FY2029, and ASML turned pre-emptive on capacity after 2Q26. ASML flagged like-for-like price increases and TSMC cited tool price inflation as a major driver of its +15% capex guide; Chinese customers reportedly accepting +10% DUV price increases.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Capex More FCF-Dilutive Than Markets Assume; Hyperscaler Spend Broadening
bullets.body: Flex Q1 FY2027 earnings and Vertiv Q2 2026 read-throughs confirm AI infrastructure investment is expanding beyond accelerators/servers into power conversion, electrical distribution, and thermal management. Flex is seeing strategic senior-level discussions across multiple hyperscalers. AI capacity expansion will be more FCF-dilutive than a chip-centric model implies. Vertiv shares fell 15% premarket on a Q2 sales miss despite strong underlying demand trends.

bullets.title: Meta's Recommendation Systems Now Scale Like LLMs, Implying Massive New Compute Demand
bullets.body: Meta's GEM foundation model demonstrates that recommendation systems — not just language models — now exhibit LLM-style scaling laws where more compute produces better performance. This suggests compute demand from recommendation workloads could extend far beyond current LLM spending, and Zuckerberg is expected to triple down on capex with potential announcement of a first compute client tonight.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Tripwire: US Sanctions Chinese Entities Over Iran Ties; Middle East Escalation Broadens
bullets.body: The US Treasury announced Iran-focused sanctions targeting Hormuz monetization and sanctioned Chinese entities over Iran ties. Israel's defense establishment believes Washington is nearing a major counter-response to Iran. China is reportedly sending rocket launchers and shoulder-launched missiles to Iran within weeks. Iraq's security council has called for legal action against US-Saudi strikes.

bullets.title: Dollar at Near-Century Low Share of FX Reserves; Bond Market Sending Warning Signals
bullets.body: The US dollar's share of global FX reserves has fallen to ~42%, down 15 percentage points since 2015 and near a century low. IG bond yields are at their highest since 2002 relative to S&P 500 earnings yields. Tech capex is a primary driver of bond market funding pressure per WSJ.

bullets.title: Credit Card Delinquencies Hit 15-Year High; Consumer Credit Stress Worsening
bullets.body: 90-day-plus credit card delinquencies reached their highest level since 2010, adding to a broadening set of macro headwinds. Mortgage qualification income requirements rose 16.7% through June 2024. Consumer credit stress is a potential transmission mechanism from tighter financial conditions to broader economic softness.

bullets.title: AI Correlated Stocks Decorrelating from Broad Market: AI Bottleneck 40 vs S&P 500 Correlation Drops to 0.01
bullets.body: The correlation between the 'AI Bottleneck 40' stocks and the remaining 460 S&P 500 companies fell to essentially zero (0.01), indicating AI leaders are now moving independently from the broader market. Multiple-sigma moves across AI long/short portfolios are causing minimal broader index movement, suggesting this is a positioning/deleveraging episode rather than a fundamental reassessment.

bullets.title: Semis Supply Chain Shift: LTA Duration Commitments Replace Margin Expansion as Key Metric
bullets.body: Analyst notes semiconductor supply chain vendors are emphasizing long-term agreement (LTA) duration commitments over margin expansion, reflecting a structural shift from prior cycles. Current supply chain constraints span the entire value chain rather than isolated segments, with LTAs across the system rather than in pockets. Unimicron providing EMIB-T scaling insights for Intel/third parties signals foundry contract normalization.

bullets.title: Busy After-Hours Catalyst Queue: MSFT, META, ARM, HOOD, CVNA All Reporting Tonight
bullets.body: Microsoft, Meta, ARM, Robinhood, and Carvana all report earnings after the close, with investor focus on Microsoft Azure growth trajectory and Meta/Microsoft capex guidance. The market is specifically watching whether Meta and Microsoft signal peak capex. Azure is reportedly growing at a record pace. Disney is reportedly switching from Microsoft GitHub Copilot to OpenAI Codex.
